entries.title: Draft: distinguish spectral conditioning from input restriction in FEI
entries.statement: DRAFT, reviewed mathematical scope note. For Boolean f let Z have law P(Z=S)=fhat(S)^2 and v=P(Z is nonempty). Spectral conditioning gives H(f)=h_2(v)+v H(Z | Z nonempty), so the factor v is essential. Input restriction at coordinate i gives the different quantity Delta_i=H(f)-[H(f_i^+)+H(f_i^-)]/2. A chain entropy H(Z_i | previously exposed spectral coordinates) is a third quantity. Counterexamples to a uniform charge for every spectral chain increment or every prescribed input split do not settle the existential-coordinate FEI induction or the universal FEI conjecture.
assumptions: Base-2 spectral entropy including the empty coefficient
v>0 when conditional law is used
Counterexample quantifiers concern every prescribed coordinate

entries.title: Draft: FEI affine and restriction boundaries
entries.statement: DRAFT, reviewed mathematical scope note. The sharp entropy-to-influence supremum for Boolean sign-reversed affine-subspace indicators is 4 (w510 C001-C002). A separate Boolean bent-plus-one-point-flip selector makes Delta_i/I_i unbounded for one prescribed coordinate (w511 C001), even though its global H/I tends to 2 and another coordinate has bounded split ratio. Both are boundary results. Neither proves or refutes the universal Fourier entropy-influence conjecture; the general mass-weighted spectral entropy budget or a suitable-coordinate selection theorem is still missing.
assumptions: The affine result applies only to affine-subspace indicators
The split obstruction concerns a prescribed coordinate

relations.rationale: The frontier distinguishes the affine mass-weighted spectrum from the prescribed input-restriction increment defined in the first card.
w510 C002 proves the affine-class constant-four supporting end; w512 independently checked the formula and limit.
w511 C001 proves the prescribed-selector obstruction; w512 independently checked its entropy and influence formulas.
w510 C003 supplies H=h_2(v)+v H(Q), with the conditional mass v retained; w512 checked the identity.
